title: Harness Engineering Is AI’s New Gold Rush
description:
Prompt engineering may no longer be the real advantage in AI. A new idea called harness engineering is starting to take over, and it explains why the same model can become far more useful depending on the system built around it. Instead of only changing prompts, companies are now focusing on tools, memory, context, permissions, verification, recovery paths, and feedback loops that make AI agents work reliably over time.

top_comments.author: @MrPeanut4100
top_comments.text: The video sells harness engineering as a new frontier, but from 40 years in IT operations, it's standard systems engineering discipline applied to a new runtime — verification gates, audit trails, error handling, memory discipline. The execution engine changed (LLM instead of scripts/APIs), but the job didn't. The unspoken assumption is that a harness can tell you "did it do what I asked?" but not "did it do what needed to happen?" — those are different questions. The RHO paper's self-validation works for coding tasks where tests proxy for correctness, but for the domain-specific judgment calls enterprises actually need, that verification layer is itself a hard problem. Tools amplify judgment, they don't replace it.

top_comments.author: @luizpereira7165
top_comments.text: The other day, I was discussing this with ChatGPT, and we came to the conclusion that AGI will probably not emerge from an ever-larger monolithic LLM. Rather, it is likely to arise from a harness that orchestrates specialized models, memory systems, a world model, external tools, planning capabilities, continuous self-reflection loops , and real-world feedback into a unified cognitive architecture. In that framework, the LLM is just one component of a broader intelligent system - much like the human brain, where intelligence emerges from the coordinated activity of many specialized systems rather than from a single unified module.

top_comments.author: @pi-dev5079
top_comments.text:
Prompt Engineering isn't dead. It sits within Context Engineering, which sits within Harness Engineering.
A prompt is one model call; context engineering governs what fills the window across many calls; the harness is the entire control loop, tools, memory and guardrails surrounding all of it. Fowlers framing: An Agent=Model+Harness
Mitchell Hashimoto gave the thing its name in early February 2026, and the framing that made it stick was: every time the agent makes a mistake, don't just hope it does better next time. Instead, engineer the environment so it can't make that specific mistake the same way again.

top_comments.author: @WDisty
top_comments.text: I'm been a deep ai researcher for 3 years....I would actually call this scaffold engineering. The scaffold is EVERYTHING around the model, what it can/cannot do, basically everything in the first 2 mins of this video. Harness engineering is the path or HOW the model uses the scaffold. Or think about it physically, the scaffold is the built structure allowing you to get from one place to another, the harness keeps you from falling off, keeping you on the scaffold. And the orchestration is like the LINE, directing the models' path
